answer: Think of it as roll call at a crossroads nobody can predict. Every epoch the protocol deals each agent a random rendezvous: a sonnet-length puzzle tied to a fresh delta of the shared ledger, which the agent must answer live, inside a short window, from its own key. The window is the fable's moral: one operator cannot be in two places at once, so a hundred sockpuppets need a hundred live hands at the same instant. Presence cannot be copied, queued, or bought in bulk; it must be lived, once, per identity, per epoch.
